The technique leverages the properties of luminance-chrominance color spaces to better align the rectification bounds with the natural distribution of color data in images [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the technique leverages luminance-chrominance color spaces to better align rectification bounds with the natural distribution of color data. Source [S1] explicitly supports this by stating: 'Performing history rectification directly in RGB color space can produce colorrelated artifacts since the RGB channels are commonly highly correlated. As seen in Figure 2.10 (a), the RGB-space AABB can become poorly aligned with the actual distribution of color samples. Transforming colors into a luminance-chrominance color space such as YCoCg or YCrCb orients the bounding box in the direction of luma... This is shown in Figure 2.10 (b), where the neighboring samples lie along the luma direction, resulting in a better fit using the YCoCg-space AABB'. This confirms that the alignment with the data distribution is the mechanism used.
